# k0rdent_security_group (Resource)

A named, ordered set of CIDR filter rules, applied to the instances of whatever it is attached to.

This is the platform's nearest thing to an address allowlist. It filters node interfaces, not the Kubernetes API endpoint, and there is no allowlist for that endpoint on the public API today.

Rules are evaluated first-match in list order, and ingress and egress are independent. Only a VPC on the `nico` fabric backend can carry security groups.

The platform adds no rules to a group. On the `nico` fabric, traffic that no rule permits is denied, in both directions. Rules the operator sets for the site are checked before the group's, so a site permit or deny wins over the group. Replies to a connection a node opened through a stateful egress rule are let back in. A change can take up to a few minutes to reach the nodes, and the cluster's Kubernetes API address isn't filtered at all.

Requires `region` and `project` on the provider.

**What replaces it.** Changing `id`, `project` or `region` cannot be done in place and replaces the security group. Everything else changes in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A baseline for every VPC, bound after the more specific groups. Egress only,
# so it lets nothing in.
resource "k0rdent_security_group" "baseline" {
  id          = "baseline"
  description = "Outbound DNS and HTTPS for every VPC."

  egress {
    name               = "dns-out"
    action             = "permit"
    protocol           = "udp"
    source_prefix      = "0.0.0.0/0"
    destination_prefix = "0.0.0.0/0"

    destination_port_range = "53"
  }

  egress {
    name               = "https-out"
    action             = "permit"
    protocol           = "tcp"
    source_prefix      = "0.0.0.0/0"
    destination_prefix = "0.0.0.0/0"

    destination_port_range = "443"
  }
}
```

```terraform
# The first matching rule wins, in the order written. On the nico fabric,
# traffic that no rule permits is denied, so the group needs no final deny.
# One would also block what the VPC's default group, checked after this one,
# permits between the VPC's subnets.
resource "k0rdent_security_group" "office_access" {
  id           = "office-access"
  display_name = "Office access"

  # Merged with the provider's `default_tags` into `tags_all`.
  tags = {
    team = "it"
  }

  ingress {
    name               = "ssh-from-office"
    action             = "permit"
    protocol           = "tcp"
    source_prefix      = "203.0.113.0/24"
    destination_prefix = "0.0.0.0/0"

    destination_port_range = "22"
  }

  # On the nico fabric, return traffic for this rule is allowed back in
  # without an ingress rule.
  egress {
    name               = "https-out"
    action             = "permit"
    protocol           = "tcp"
    source_prefix      = "0.0.0.0/0"
    destination_prefix = "0.0.0.0/0"

    destination_port_range = "443"
  }

  # Ingress rules are stateless, so the SSH replies need a rule of their own.
  egress {
    name               = "ssh-replies"
    action             = "permit"
    protocol           = "tcp"
    source_prefix      = "0.0.0.0/0"
    destination_prefix = "203.0.113.0/24"

    source_port_range = "22"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-form text describing it, for people to read.
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name. Free text, not unique.
- `egress` (Block List) Rules filtering traffic leaving the instance, in evaluation order.

Rules are stateless, with one exception the platform applies on the `nico` fabric: an egress `tcp` or `udp` rule with a `destination_port_range` and no `source_port_range` is made stateful, so return traffic does not need a matching ingress rule. It is a property of the enforcement and is not reported back, so nothing in this schema can show it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--egress))
- `id` (String) Group name, unique in the project among live groups. Omit it and the provider generates one, `tf-` and 16 hex digits, so that a create whose answer is lost can be read back rather than sent twice.

A group mid-teardown keeps its name: recreating one with the same `id` is refused with `409` until the old one has finished deleting. **Forces replacement**. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL. String length must be at most 63.
- `ingress` (Block List) Rules filtering traffic arriving at the instance, in evaluation order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--ingress))
- `project` (String) Project this resource belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project`. It's part of the resource's API path, so a resource can't move between projects. **Forces replacement**. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `region` (String) Region this resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `region`. It's part of the resource's API path, so a resource can't move between regions. **Forces replacement**. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `tags` (Map of String) User-defined labels. The contract types tag values as freeform JSON; this schema accepts strings, because a Terraform map has one element type and a string is the only one every value round-trips through. **Constraints:** The key `terraform-provider-k0rdent/create-token` is the provider's own.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) How long each operation may take before it fails. Each operation left out defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `owner_kind` (String) Set to `vpc` when the platform owns this group rather than the tenant: a VPC's DEFAULT group. Such a group cannot be modified or deleted, so a value here means this resource cannot manage what it is pointed at.
- `rule_count` (Number) Rules in the group, ingress plus egress, as the platform counts them. A write is refused when it would push this above 256.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this group.
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state as last read from the platform.
- `tags_all` (Map of String) Every tag the platform holds for this resource: the provider's `default_tags` with this resource's own `tags` on top, a resource tag winning over a default with the same key. Known at plan whenever both are, so the plan shows the result. The provider's create token never appears here.

<a id="nestedblock--egress"></a>
### Nested Schema for `egress`

Required:

- `action` (String) `permit` or `deny`. Lowercase: an uppercase spelling is rejected, not normalised. **Constraints:** Value must be one of: ["permit" "deny"].
- `destination_prefix` (String) Destination range in CIDR notation. See `source_prefix`. **Constraints:** Must be a CIDR prefix with all host bits zero, such as `10.0.0.0/24`.
- `protocol` (String) `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `icmp6` or `any`. `icmp6` is distinct from `icmp`: a rule written for one does not match the other. Only `tcp` and `udp` may carry ports. **Constraints:** Value must be one of: ["tcp" "udp" "icmp" "icmp6" "any"].
- `source_prefix` (String) Source range in CIDR notation, with host bits zero. Both prefixes are required: a rule that constrains one side is written with `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0` on the other, so the intent is in the rule rather than in an omission. **Constraints:** Must be a CIDR prefix with all host bits zero, such as `10.0.0.0/24`.

Optional:

- `destination_port_range` (String) As `source_port_range`, for the destination side. **Constraints:** Must be a port (`"80"`) or an inclusive range (`"80-81"`).
- `name` (String) A label for the rule. Free text, not unique, and not used for ordering: position in the list is the only ordering signal. At most 253 characters. **Constraints:** String length must be at most 253.
- `source_port_range` (String) A single port (`"80"`) or an inclusive range (`"80-81"`), as a string. Omit it to match any source port. Valid only on `tcp` and `udp`. **Constraints:** Must be a port (`"80"`) or an inclusive range (`"80-81"`).

- `protocol` (String) `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `icmp6` or `any`. `icmp6` is distinct from `icmp`: a rule written for one does not match the other. Only `tcp` and `udp` may carry ports. **Constraints:** Value must be one of: ["tcp" "udp" "icmp" "icmp6" "any"].

Both prefixes are required: a rule that constrains one side is written with `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0` on the other, so the intent is in the rule rather than in an omission. **Constraints:** Must be a CIDR prefix with all host bits zero, such as `10.0.0.0/24`.

- `name` (String) A label for the rule. Free text, not unique, and not used for ordering: position in the list is the only ordering signal. At most 253 characters. **Constraints:** String length must be at most 253.
- `source_port_range` (String) A single port (`"80"`) or an inclusive range (`"80-81"`), as a string. Omit it to match any source port. Valid only on `tcp` and `udp`. **Constraints:** Must be a port (`"80"`) or an inclusive range (`"80-81"`).


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Bounds the whole create, including the wait until the platform reports it ready. Left out, it defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. **Constraints:** Must be a positive duration of hours, minutes or seconds, such as `45m`, `2h` or `1h30m`.
- `delete` (String) Bounds the whole destroy, including the wait until the platform reports it gone. Left out, it defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. **Constraints:** Must be a positive duration of hours, minutes or seconds, such as `45m`, `2h` or `1h30m`.
- `update` (String) Bounds the whole update, including the wait until the platform settles. Left out, it defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. **Constraints:** Must be a positive duration of hours, minutes or seconds, such as `45m`, `2h` or `1h30m`.

## Timeouts

The `timeouts` block sets how long each operation may take before it fails:

- `create` (default `2h`). Bounds the whole create, including the wait until the platform reports it ready.
- `update` (default `2h`). Bounds the whole update, including the wait until the platform settles.
- `delete` (default `2h`). Bounds the whole destroy, including the wait until the platform reports it gone.

Each default is the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. An operation the block leaves out takes that value, so raising `operation_timeout` raises all of them at once. A value of zero or less is refused at plan time rather than read as no limit.

A wait that runs out, or a run that is interrupted, stops nothing on the platform. A create that stops waiting fails, and Terraform taints the object: run `terraform untaint` on it and then `terraform apply`, which waits for the same object. A delete that stops waiting fails and stays in state, and the next `terraform destroy` waits for the same delete without sending another.

```terraform
resource "k0rdent_security_group" "example" {
  # ...

  timeouts {
    create = "45m"
    update = "45m"
    delete = "45m"
  }
}
```

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# The same address with each part named. Leave out region and project to
# use the provider's.
import {
  to = k0rdent_security_group.example
  identity = {
    region  = "us-texas-1"
    project = "cp-production"
    id      = "office-access"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The resource's id.

#### Optional

- `project` (String) Project the resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `project` on import.
- `region` (String) Region the resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `region` on import.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Takes every id form `terraform import` does. The first command below uses
# the provider's region and project, the second names them.
import {
  to = k0rdent_security_group.example
  id = "us-texas-1/cp-production/office-access"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import k0rdent_security_group.example office-access

terraform import k0rdent_security_group.example us-texas-1/cp-production/office-access
```
